messages.subject: Re: R graphics won't refresh using plot(x)
messages.subject_clean: R graphics won't refresh using plot(x)
messages.body_plain:
On Jan 5, 2009, at 7:24 , Graham Etherington wrote:

> Hi,
> I'm constructing my Rengine as follows:
>
> Rengine re = new Rengine (null, true, new JRITextConsole ());
>
> and I'm using the sample code in rtest.java that came in the JRI  
> example
> code to construct the JRITextConsole().
> I am however just producing R graphics directly and not using JGR. Is
> this a problem? I don't particularly want any 'interaction' from my
> graphics. I just want them to display things like phylogenetic trees,
> dendograms, convex hulls, etc. Do I really need to use JGR for that?

This has nothing to do with JGR per se - I was just suggesting you  
look at JGR source code to see how it's done properly, you don't need  
to actually use JGR.

he "interaction" you want from your graphics is redraw on resize. That  
can only be done if that graphics you use support callbacks to R and  
(depending on the device) you have the event loop running. You didn't  
tell us in any e-mail what graphics device you're actually using, so  
all here is speculation, but I can only repeat - have a look at JavaGD  
since that it a native Java device - you'll have hard time integrating  
any non-Java device in your JRI app.

Cheers,
Simon


>
> On Mon, 2008-12-29 at 09:53 -0500, Simon Urbanek wrote:
>>> Hi,
>>> I'm producing graphs/plots using the following code as an example
>>> (re = org.rosuda.JRI.Rengine):
>>>
>>> #code starts
>>> re.eval ("library (ape)");
>>> re.eval ("tree_mr <- nj(r_matrix)");
>>> re.eval ("plot(tree_mr)");
>>> #code ends
>>>
>>> The graph is produced and looks fine, but if I reduce the graph to a
>>> minimised icon and then maximise it, the graph is blank. The same
>>> thing happens if I move another window across the graph - wherever
>>> the window moves over the graph it appears to 'rub out' that part of
>>> the graph as the image below the window does not re-appear once
>>> exposed again.
>>>
>>> I'm using JDK 1.6, JRI 0.4.1 and R version 2.7.2 Patched (2008-09-02
>>> r46484) on Linux.
>>> If I run the code outside of JRI (e.g. through the R command line
>>> interface), the graphics behave properly.
>>>
>>> I was wondering if anyone had run into this problem before or if
>>> anyone had any suggestions.
>>>
>>
>> Apparently you're not running an event loop and/or you are using non-
>> Java graphics. If you want an interactive environment (e.g. full
>> console etc.), you should run the REPL - see startMainLoop() method
>> and R documentation. Also you really don't want to use non-Java
>> interactive graphics devices in JRI, because they don't integrate  
>> well
>> with the UI, so  make sure you're using JavaGD (see JGR for details
>> how to integrate everything seamlessly).
>>
>> Cheers,
>> Simon
>>
> Dr. Graham Etherington
> Post-doctoral Bioinformatician,
> Computational and Systems Biology,
> The John Innes Centre,
> Norwich Research Park,
> Norwich NR4 7UH,
> UK

messages.subject: Feature request/bug-report
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

First of all I would like to thank the authors of JGR for providing a 
beuatiful interface for using R in both Linux and windows. I have just 
learned about the existence of the program, but I am already very 
impressed about the simple and effective set of features it provides.

However, I think there seems to be one major thing missing. I does not 
seem like there is a shortcut for evaluating a line and step one line 
inside the script editor (corresponding to e.g. F5 in the windows R 
gui). Can this be true? I know about Ctrl+ENTER but that only evaluates 
the line. To evaluate multiple lines it seems like you have to press 
Ctrl+ENTER and arrow down again and again or mark the lines and then 
press Ctrl+ENTER.  This seems like a silly thing to leave out in such a 
great programme. Also I think it would be great to have a short-cut to 
evaluate a section of lines, where the section is separated by blank 
lines. I may just be to new, so if these short-cuts exist I would be 
very glad to learn about them.

I also have a bug-report regarding the Ctrl+ENTER shortcut. I have 
installed the latest version of JGR with R 2.6 on windows XP SP2, and 
here Ctrl+ENTER simply does not seem to work at all...?

Kind regards,
Stig Mortensen

But have you installed 64-bit R and 64-bit JRI? Note that the CRAN  
binary version of rJava contains only 32-bit JRI, so you have to  
install a 64-bit version of JRI (which is not the default even for 64- 
bit rJava - unfortunately). This should do the trick:

Sys.setenv("FORCE_NATIVE"=1)
install.packages("rJava",type='source')

Cheers,
Simon

"?" is interpreted by JGR (re-mapped to internal call to help followed  
by help.search if no topics were found) instead of R. So JGR is  
smarter than R used to be, but that has changed in R 2.8.  
Unfortunately R has currently no publicly available API to support  
what the Mac-GUI does, because it uses a nasty trick by modifying R's  
sources to hook inside R. I'm working on fixing this for R 2.9.0-to- 
be, but currently JGR is out of luck and has to rely on its own  
attempts to parse the command line, so the results will vary until then.
